test_title: PYST 34: SSC CHSL 2024 - English (Held On: 11 Jul, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence.

I know Covid has made you terribly ill, but __the good thing__ is that you have developed immunity against it for further infections.

options.text: the silver lining in the cloud

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"the silver lining in the cloud"** means finding something positive in an otherwise negative situation. (किसी नकारात्मक स्थिति में कुछ सकारात्मक खोजना)

 
 
• **Example: **Even though he lost his job, he found** the silver lining in the cloud** by starting his own business.
 
 
 
• **Immunity** refers to the ability to resist a particular infection or toxin by the action of specific antibodies or sensitized white blood cells. (प्रतिरक्षा)
 
 
• **Example: **Vaccinations help build immunity against various diseases.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Being in the quicksilver** (पारा के संपर्क में होना): This phrase is not commonly used as an idiom in English.
 
• **Crossing palms with silver** (किसी को रिश्वत देना): This phrase means to bribe someone.
 
 
• **Example:** He crossed the official’s palms with silver to get the work done quickly.
 
 
 
• **The silver spoon** (चांदी का चम्मच): This phrase is used to indicate someone born into wealth and privilege.
 
 
• **Example:** She was born with a silver spoon in her mouth and never had to worry about money.
 
 

42:Tc84,
The correct answer is **Option 3**.
